title: Consolidate request paths and cache lifecycle management for Console API
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: The Console backend has accumulated overlapping aggregation endpoints and ad-hoc cache layers added over multiple sprints. Resulting issues: duplicated GraphQL resolvers that make separate REST calls for the same underlying analytics data, inconsistent TTLs causing cache churn, and excessive memcached/Redis churn during spikes. Symptom metrics: dashboard page p95 go from 420ms to 1.6s under medium load; API request count to analytics microservice up 4x; Redis key churn spikes during release windows. Root causes: (1) multiple teams added thin aggregation endpoints instead of reusing a single coordinator service, (2) resolver-level caching uses heterogeneous keys and TTLs, (3) caching lifecycle lacks coordinated invalidation hooks for write events (rollouts, model updates), (4) code paths mix in-memory caches (per-node) with centralized Redis without clear ownership.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end Console API latency and backend load by consolidating request aggregation, standardizing cache keying/TTL, and implementing robust invalidation lifecycle. Target: p95 dashboard latency <= 400ms under the 95th percentile of current load, and reduce redundant calls to analytics service by at least 60%.

Proposed approach: 1) Introduce a single aggregation coordinator endpoint (/internal/v1/console-aggregate) that accepts a batched descriptor of UI sections and returns a single consolidated payload. 2) Refactor GraphQL resolvers to call the coordinator instead of making independent REST calls; add a lightweight translation layer for backwards compatibility. 3) Implement a standardized cache layer in Redis with a namespaced key format (console:{env}:{view}:{component}:{hash}) and TTL strategy (short-lived 30s sliding for volatile widgets, 10m for stable counts). 4) Add server-side cache lifecycle hooks: publish invalidation events to an internal pub/sub (Kafka) when writes occur and process them in a debounced invalidation worker. 5) Deprecate per-node in-memory caches for aggregation data; keep in-memory for ephemeral request-scoped memoization only. 6) Add feature-flagged canary rollout and gradual traffic shift with Circuit Breaker fallback to individual endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard p95 latency <= 400ms on canary region under baseline load tests
>= 60% reduction in duplicate downstream requests to analytics service measured over 24h
Cache invalidation events observed in Kafka with <5s propagation to invalidation worker
No increase in error rate (>0.2%) during canary rollout; automatic rollback on breach
All updated resolvers covered by unit tests and integration tests; PRs have two approvals
tasks: Design: finalize coordinator request schema and backwards-compat translation document (Confluence: /docs/console/aggregate-schema)
Infra: provision a Redis namespace and increase maxclients for canary cluster
Backend: implement /internal/v1/console-aggregate (Node service) with batching and parallel fetch orchestration
Backend: refactor GraphQL resolvers to call aggregation endpoint behind a feature flag
Cache: implement standardized key builder and TTL policy; add metrics (hits/misses, ttl distribution)
Invalidation: add write-side publishers for updates (Kafka topic: console-cache-inval) and build debounced invalidation worker
Tests: create k6 load script and synthetic scenarios that reproduce current cache churn
Observability: add tracing spans for aggregation coordinator and dashboards in Grafana; add SLO alert for console p95
Rollout: canary with 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic steps and automated rollback policy
